statement: For a separated quasi-finite étale group over a locally noetherian base, fibre order is lower semicontinuous; local constancy of the order gives local finiteness. The proof reduces to a trait and injects the special fibre group into the generic fibre after a suitable strictly henselian/completed reduction.

statement: The literal claim that W_G(R) is a subquotient of W_G(T) for any nested tori is false. For G=SL4(C), R has cocharacter (3,1,−1,−3), while T is the connected kernel in the diagonal torus of character (1,2,−7,4); then R⊂T, W_G(R)=C2 and W_G(T)=1. The usual proof works when T is maximal.

statement: A torus commuting with a maximal torus lies in it. Under the stated smooth finite-presentation and locally constant reductive-rank hypotheses, commutative/nilpotent fibres have the described unique/central maximal tori; conjugacy is étale local. For G⊃H⊃T with equal reductive ranks, maximality in G is equivalent to maximality in H. The zero-unipotent-rank locus is open. The converse existence over artinian bases or locally reductive groups is deferred to XIV.

statement: A reductive centre is a central multiplicative-type subgroup with the universal factorization property after base change. With affine-fibre hypotheses the fibrewise condition gives the universal one; affine algebraic groups over fields have such a centre. The centre of the quotient by the full reductive centre is trivial under the stated smooth connected hypotheses. A literal intersection formula on23 is ill-typed and some references/parts are absent.

statement: For a smooth algebraic group over a field and a maximal torus T, the Weyl quotient N_G(T)/C_G(T) is finite étale; its geometric points are the abstract geometric Weyl group and commute with field extension.

statement: For a field F of characteristic≠2, Delzant’s Q(F) is the Grothendieck–Witt ring of nondegenerate finite-dimensional quadratic forms, not the Witt ring. Diagonal rank-one forms generate it and the kernel of Z[F*/F*²]→GW(F) is generated by the binary isometry relations stated in the offprint.

check_reason: The monoid group completion and binary relation proof identify the exact object and prevent dropping the rank coordinate.

statement: The rank-zero ideal J⊂GW(F) maps isomorphically to the fundamental ideal I⊂W(F), hence J^r→I^r. For d_a=⟨a⟩−1, the degree-two Stiefel–Whitney class of d_a d_b equals (a)∪(b), and J³ maps to zero in degrees≤2.

statement: Delzant uses a filtered total-class ring retaining rank. Rank-one forms map to their Kummer classes; the construction is natural under field homomorphisms. The Clifford invariant is normalized relative to the same-rank unit form. If the displayed untilded target were read as omitting rank, injectivity would be false, e.g. ⟨1⟩ and ⟨1,1⟩ have identical positive classes.

statement: Over a number field, a quadratic form is determined by its rank and all cohomological Stiefel–Whitney classes. Local finite places use dimension, discriminant and Clifford invariant; at real places the total class recovers the number of negative squares through binary binomial coefficients, and Hasse’s principle globalizes.
